title: Dtypes and shape
summary: One type per array, and arrays with rows and columns.

steps.title: Every array has one dtype
body: All elements of an array share one **dtype** (data type). NumPy picks the narrowest type that
One type is what makes arrays fast and compact. It is also a trap: a single stray string in
a column of numbers turns the whole array into text, and maths stops working.

steps.explain: One float is enough to make every element a float: `3` became `3.0`.

steps.title: Changing dtype with astype
body: `.astype(new_type)` returns a **new** array converted to another type:
Converting float to int **chops off** the decimals rather than rounding. Round first if
you mean rounding. You will also meet `float32` / `int32`: half the memory, less precision.

steps.explain: `astype(int)` truncates toward zero. To round, call `.round()` first (and note NumPy rounds halves to even: `0.5` becomes `0.0`).

steps.title: Shape: rows and columns
body: Arrays can have more than one dimension. A 2-D array is a table: `shape` is `(rows, columns)`.
`reshape` never changes the number of elements, so the new shape must multiply to the same

steps.explain: `g[1]` is the second row. `-1` asks NumPy to compute that dimension: 12 / 6 = 2.
The shape must multiply to 12, and only one dimension may be `-1`.

steps.title: Numbers from text
prompt: Data often arrives as text. Write `parse_scores(text)` that takes a string of
space-separated numbers and returns an **integer** array of the values **rounded** to the
Split the text, convert with `astype(float)` (or `dtype=float`), round, then `astype(int)`.
template: Dojo.check("dtype is an integer type", _np.issubdtype(_np.asarray(_r).dtype, _np.integer), "dtype is " + str(_np.asarray(_r).dtype))

steps.title: Reshape into a grid
prompt: Write `as_grid(values, cols)` that turns a flat list into a 2-D array with `cols` columns
If the values do not fill whole rows, raise `ValueError` yourself with a clear message,
for example `"6 values do not fill rows of 4"`.
solution: raise ValueError(f"{a.size} values do not fill rows of {cols}")
hints: `a.size % cols` tells you whether rows are full.
`a.reshape(-1, cols)` computes the number of rows.
template: Dojo.throws("6 values in rows of 4 raises ValueError", ValueError, lambda: as_grid([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], 4))
